question: A can complete a job in 36 days. Every third day, he is assisted by B who can complete the job alone in 48 days. In how many days will the job be completed?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 36, 48) = 144 units.

Efficiency: A = 4, B = 3.

3-day cycle work (A + A + A&B) = 4 + 4 + 7 = 15 units.

In 27 days (9 cycles), work = 9 × 15 = 135 units. Remainder = 9 units.

Day 28 & 29 (A works) = 4 + 4 = 8 units. Remainder = 1 unit.

Time for last 1 unit = 1/7 day. Total = 27 + 2 + 1/7 = 29 1/7 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 29 1/7 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 36 days

Time taken by B = 48 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken by individuals

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM(36, 48) = 144 units.

⇒ Efficiency of A = 144 ÷ 36 = 4 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 144 ÷ 48 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Work pattern (3-day cycle): Day 1 (A), Day 2 (A), Day 3 (A+B).

⇒ Work in 1 cycle = 4 + 4 + (4 + 3) = 15 units.

⇒ Total cycles = 144 ÷ 15 = 9 cycles + 9 units remaining.

⇒ Time for 9 cycles = 9 × 3 = 27 days.

⇒ Work on Day 28 (A works) = 4 units. Remaining = 9 − 4 = 5 units.

⇒ Work on Day 29 (A works) = 4 units. Remaining = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

⇒ Time for remaining 1 unit on Day 30 (A+B work) = 1 ÷ 7 days.

⇒ Total time = 27 + 1 + 1 + 1/7 = 29 1/7 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 29 1/7 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days or 3 days) and then divide the total work by the cycle work.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person, which is equivalent to the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p
